case.title: Science fair venue, budget and volunteers

canvasName: R3-C06 Science fair venue, budget and volunteers

segments.text: Thank you for coming to the science fair planning meeting. We have about forty minutes and we need to leave with a budget, a schedule, a venue plan, and named owners. The fair is for grades six through eight, it will run on a Saturday in October, and we expect one hundred and twenty student projects. Last year we had eighty projects and it was already crowded, so this year we need a different layout.
segments.textReply: Captured the meeting goals and scale: grades 6–8, Saturday in October, 120 projects—up from last year’s crowded 80—and the need for a new layout.

segments.text: Let's start with the goal. The fair should be a low pressure opportunity for students to explain their work, not a pure competition. Every student gets a table and a short presentation slot. We will have three judged categories: scientific method, engineering design, and communication. We also want a family open house in the afternoon so parents and younger students can visit.
segments.textReply: Added the low-pressure presentation goal, the three judged categories, and an afternoon family open house.

segments.text: Last year we spent two thousand on tables, six hundred on printing, four hundred on awards, and three hundred on snacks. This year we want to add a keynote speaker and a livestream for families who cannot attend. The speaker honorarium is five hundred, the AV rental is seven hundred, and the livestream requires a volunteer and a dedicated laptop. Let's compare the two realistic venue plans.

The known prior spend plus keynote and AV totals $4,500—$500 above the $4,000 PTA baseline, before venue costs or fundraising. shapes.title: School science fair · post-session summary
shapes.html:
School science fair · decisions & follow-through
Purpose: plan a welcoming grades 6–8 fair for up to 120 projects, with a workable venue, schedule, budget and named owners.
Decisions
Venue: Plan A — school gym + courtyard; quiet corner and small entrance PA. Atrium is backup only if gym unavailable.
Capacity: registration capped at 120 projects. Gym access at 6 a.m. depends on request ≥2 weeks ahead.
Budget: approve $3,100; hold $900 contingency from $4,000 PTA funds. Receipts due within 2 weeks.
Format: low-pressure student presentations, with judged categories for scientific method, engineering design and communication; afternoon family open house.
Core plan & safeguards
Engineering projects near courtyard; reading/communication in quiet corner. Use small PA, not gym sound system; generators kept away from tables. Two speakers, six mics.
Teacher sponsor + safety form required at registration; heat/chemical/live-animal projects need teacher-signed pre-approval. No open flames; grounded outlets; no daisy-chained strips; two first-aid stations; emergency path clear.
Accessibility: temporary courtyard ramp; front row reserved for wheelchairs/strollers; ask access needs on registration.

Judges rotate in pairs, ≤12 projects per pair. Presentations: 15-minute slots + 5-minute transitions.
Risks & checkpoints
Volunteer coverage is the largest risk: judges 6/12, check-in 2/4, first aid 0/2 stated, floaters 0/2 stated, AV lead 0/1 stated. Livestream also needs a volunteer + dedicated laptop.
